answer: A sponsor quota with joint slashing blocks bulk fakes. An applicant locks a stake on a glacier schedule while a sponsor vouches from a grove quota of ten. A verifier checks quota and a fresh dune receipt tied to one device; cheating slashes the stake and revokes the quota. The k-th fake costs 40+12k units: quota scarcity and joint-slash risk grow with n, cannot be reused, verifiers enforce it, and failure loses stake plus quota. One fake costs 52 units, 1000 cost 6,046,000. A rented-history farm fails when shared dune receipts trigger joint slash. Honest agents pay once.
